title: Travelling the world with Ella; Norman Granz
summary: His largest travelling came with Ella; Norman Granz treated musicians well.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, so you went all over the world with Ella.
Oh, yeah, that's where I did most all of my travelling, with her. That's where all of my biggest travelling.
So you never played anything but houses of wild enthusiasm.
That's right, that's right.
And Norman handled you very nicely, I think. Everybody travelled very nicely, and --
He's a great cat. I like him.
Do you?
Yes.
He's egotistical.
Well, I guess so.
Who isn't, you mean?
Who isn't? Everybody got their ways, but --
First of all, he appreciates the music. He knows what he's listening to.
He knows what he's listening to. And he know his business.
Yeah.
That's one thing.
Yeah.
He knows his business.
And he does think the artist should be treated just right.
That's right, that's right.
Which nobody else is really in that ball game.
I've never had any trouble with him.
That's not George Wein, is it?
I don't know, I never had trouble with Wein, either, but everybody else has.
Everybody else has, yeah.
But I never had no trouble with him Gran z. or with the Norman Grants.
Oh, well, that's -- I'm not surprised you didn't have --
Norman would say, 'You want this? You want that? Do that, and that's that.'
Yeah.
And no problems whatsoever.
You must have enjoyed it. You and Tommy together.
I did, I did.
